question: Attribute the ordered road round cost before changing the algorithm.

interactive_extension.purpose: Earlier distributed round-cost attribution while the eight-node cells wait in cpu; an intermediate scale, not a substitute for the eight-node endpoint.
interactive_extension.parameters: Same frozen binaries, sources, per-node layout, repetitions, old scheduler and acceptance checks as the original protocol.
interactive_extension.limits: At most four nodes, one hour, one running job and two submitted jobs per user; this campaign keeps its existing 20-minute limit.

predictions.condition: controller logging seconds / instrumented solve seconds >= 0.20
predictions.otherwise: output sensitivity only; no automatic promotion

predictions.condition: 267-long unloaded round cost / real production round cost >= 0.50
267-long unloaded round cost / real production round cost < 0.25
predictions.action: investigate threshold handling and loaded queue delay

acceptance: Independent full digests, old-scheduler startup confirmation, work conservation. One matched intervention, then a second allocation and regression checks before acceptance.
caveats: Nested phase timings are inclusive; PE-time sums are not wall-clock critical paths.
Unloaded cycles omit graph work and idle callbacks; do not subtract as communication time.
Suppressing output can alter asynchronous work and rounds; report both.

layout_decision.reason: User reports prior full-solver comparisons on other machines found 16x7 best. Unloaded-cycle measurements do not justify another layout sweep; keep 16x7 fixed.

next_contribution_screen.hypothesis: current_thresholds queues hold release and heap draining, then immediately snapshots the histogram. Taking the snapshot after one bounded local work turn may reduce feedback lag and rounds.
next_contribution_screen.evidence_limit: Unchanged thresholds are not empty rounds: most still create or retire updates. This experiment must demonstrate lower solve time rather than just fewer polls.
correctness_requirements: One contribution per PE per epoch, including idle PEs
Bound local work by existing slice; do not wait for queue exhaustion
Serial digests and work accounting before timing
next_contribution_screen.screen: Two training sources, one node first, one warmup and three measured launches, interleaved baseline/candidate/repeated-baseline arms. Same graph and source settings as this protocol.
next_contribution_screen.acceptance: Road speedup >=1.05 beyond control variation, edge work within 20%; mesh speedup >=0.95 and within control noise if below 1. Second allocation and held-out confirmation required for acceptance.
next_contribution_screen.stop_rule: Reject if rounds fall without solve-time benefit or work/regression limits fail; no open-ended timer, layout or width sweep.
next_contribution_screen.distributed_followup: Keep the eight-node endpoint in cpu if warranted; user declined reducing it to four nodes.
